paper.title: Functional multi-armed bandit and the best function identification problems

unmapped: Each arm is a separate convex optimisation problem f_i on a convex set X_i in R^{n_i}; the action is a pair (index i_t, point x in X_i) and regret is sum_t f_{i_t}(x_t) - min_i min_x f_i
Learner knows the convergence-rate function g_i (and its constants M_i, R_i) of a base optimiser for each arm
settings.definition_quote: Given convex objective functions $f_1,\ldots,f_K$ and convex decision sets ... the agent chooses index $i_t$ and the decision vector $x^{t,i_t}$; the agent receives oracle feedback $\mathcal{O}_{i_t}(x^{t,i_t})$, e.g., gradient ... $R_O(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T [f_{i_t}(x^{t,i_t}) - f^*]$

unmapped: Each arm is a separate convex optimisation problem; action = (index, point); regret relative to the global minimum over arms
Learner knows the convergence-rate function g_i (constants L_i, R_i) of each base optimiser

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic FMAB, mu-strongly convex M-Lipschitz functions
unmapped: Each arm is a separate convex optimisation problem; action = (index, point)
Learner knows the convergence-rate function g_i (constants M_i, mu_i) of each base optimiser

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic FMAB, mu-strongly convex L-smooth functions
unmapped: Each arm is a separate convex optimisation problem; action = (index, point)
Learner knows the convergence-rate function g_i (constants R_i, kappa_i) of each base optimiser

settings.name_in_paper: Deterministic FMAB with g_i(k)-bounded base optimisers
unmapped: Each arm is an optimisation problem equipped with an oracle and a base algorithm with known deterministic convergence rate g_i(k) (oracle type generic)
Learner knows g_i for each arm
settings.definition_quote: An algorithm is called a $g(k, \delta)$-bounded algorithm if ... $f(x_k) - f(x^*) \leq g(k, \delta)$ ... If there exists a function $g(k)$ such that $f(x_k) - f(x^*) \leq g(k)$, we say that the algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ is $g(k)$-bounded.

unmapped: Each arm is a separate convex optimisation problem accessed through a black-box oracle; the learner outputs an index J_T and regret is min_x f_{J_T}(x) - f^*
All K problems belong to a common class F with oracle-complexity function g; learner knows g_i of each base optimiser
settings.definition_quote: At the end of $T$ rounds, the agent selects an arm, denoted by $J_T$, and aims to minimize the regret $R_B(T) = \min_{x \in \mathcal{X}_{J_T}} f_{J_T} (x) - f^*$

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic FMAB with g_i(k,delta)-bounded base optimisers (inexact oracles)
unmapped: Each arm is an optimisation problem with an inexact (stochastic) oracle and a base optimiser with high-probability rate g_i(k,delta)
Functions bounded above by A (Assumption 1); learner knows A (used to set delta) and g_i
settings.definition_quote: This section presents bounds for regrets $R_O$ and $R_B$, if $g_i(k, \delta)$-bounded base optimizers use inexact oracles. ... Functions $f_i$ are bounded above, i.e. $\max_{1 \leq i \leq K}\max_{x_i \in D_i}f_i(x_i) \leq A$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic FMAB, convex L-smooth, heavy-tailed gradient noise
unmapped: Heavy tails are on the stochastic gradient oracle: E||G_i(x,xi)-grad f_i(x)||^alpha <= sigma^alpha, alpha in (1,2]
Functions bounded above by A; learner knows A, sigma, L, R through g(k,delta)
settings.definition_quote: The algorithm $\mathcal{A}_i$ has access to the unbiased stochastic first-order oracle, returning $G_i(x, \xi)$. There exists a set~$\mathcal{X}_i$ and values $\sigma \geq 0, \alpha \in (1, 2]$ such that ... $\mathbb{E}_\xi [\|  G_i(x, \xi) - \nabla f_i(x)\|^\alpha ] \leq \sigma^\alpha$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic FMAB, mu-strongly convex L-smooth, heavy-tailed gradient noise
unmapped: Heavy tails are on the stochastic gradient oracle (alpha-th moment bound sigma^alpha)
Functions bounded above by A; learner knows A and g(k,delta)

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic FMAB, mu-strongly convex M-Lipschitz, sub-Gaussian gradient noise
unmapped: Sub-Gaussian noise is on the stochastic gradient oracle (Assumptions 2 with alpha=2 and 3)
Functions bounded above by A; learner knows A and g(k,delta)
settings.definition_quote: For any $x$ we have: $\mathbb{E} \exp\{\| G_i(x, \xi) - \nabla f_i(x) \|^2 /\sigma_i^2\} \leq 1.$

source.label: thm:lb-bfi
source.quote: For any BFI algorithm and any $T \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists a family $\{P_i\}_{i=1}^K \subset \mathcal{F}$ such that $R_B(T) \ge \underline g^{-1}\!\left(\frac{T}{K}\right)$, where $\underline g^{-1}$ is the functional inverse of $\underline g$.

results.notes: Restated as Theorem 6 in the appendix. Dimensionally odd (inverse of g applied to T/K, likely meant g(T/K)); recorded as stated.

symbols.t_eps: vicinity hitting time t(epsilon) = min{t : g(H,t) <= epsilon} for the class lower-bound function

conditions: K = 2 problems from a class with uniform sharp lower bound function g(H,t)

source.quote: Consider the best function identification problem consisting of two  problems from a given class with uniform sharp lower bound function $g(H, t)$. Then achieving regret $R_B(T) \leq \varepsilon$ requires at least $T \geq  2 \cdot t(\varepsilon)$ testing points.

results.notes: Number of oracle calls needed to guarantee R_B <= epsilon. Extension to K arms is only stated as an Assumption (Assumption 4), not recorded.

conditions: homogeneous case: all P_i share the same hardness

source.label: thm:lb-fmab_app
source.quote: For any FMAB algorithm and any $T\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists a family $\{P_i\}_{i=1}^K \subset \mathcal{F}$ such that $R_O(T)\ge \inf_{\{k_i\ge 0: \sum k_i=T\}} \sum_{i=1}^K G(k_i)$. ... (i) Convex $M$-Lipschitz: ... $\Rightarrow R_O(T)=\Omega(MR\sqrt{T})$

results.notes: Paper's M = Lipschitz constant (L_lip), R = diameter (diam_K). Also stated after Theorem 2 in main text. General form inf sum G(k_i) not recorded separately. Remark 5 claims Omega(MR sqrt(KT)) for 'fairly exploring' algorithms (informal).
Paper's L (smoothness) mapped to beta, R to diam_K.

source.label: thm:lb-fmab_app
source.quote:
(iii) $\mu$-strongly convex, $M$-Lipschitz: $\underline g(s)=\Omega\!\bigl(M^2/(\mu s)\bigr)
   \ \Rightarrow\ G(m)=\Omega\!\bigl((M^2/\mu)\log m\bigr) \Rightarrow R_O(T)=\Omega\!\bigl((M^2/\mu)\log T\bigr)$,

results.notes: Paper's mu (strong convexity) mapped to alpha.

source.label: thm:lb-fmab_app
source.quote: (iv) $\mu$-strongly convex, $L$-smooth: $\underline g(s)=\Omega(R^2 e^{-s/\sqrt{\kappa}}) \Rightarrow G(m)=\Omega(R^2) \Rightarrow R_O(T)=\Omega( R^2 )$

source.label: thm:regret_alpha
source.quote: Let $r > 0$. Assume $\mathcal{A}_i$ are $g_i(k)$-bounded base algorithms with $g_i(k) = \frac{\beta_i}{k^r}$. Then for Algorithm~\ref{alg:f_ucb}, for all $\tau$ ... if $r \in (0, 1)$: $R_O(\tau) \leq  O((\sum_{i=1}^K \beta_i^{\frac{1}{r}})^{r} \tau^{1-r})$

results.notes: Holds for all tau <= T; tau written as T.

source.label: th:bfi_det_bound
source.quote: Consider a deterministic BFI problem. ... To achieve regret $R_B(T) \leq\varepsilon$, Algorithm \ref{alg:f_ucb} requires at most $T = 1+\sum_{i=1}^k g_i^{-1}(\max[f_i^*-f^* - \frac{\varepsilon}{2}, \frac{\varepsilon}{2}])$ iterations

results.notes: Table 1 specialises this to PGD/AGD for four function classes (not recorded separately).

symbols.beta_i: constant of arm i's rate g_i(k)=beta_i/k^r

source.quote: If for each base algorithm $g_i(k)=\frac{\beta_i}{k^{r}}$ with $r>0,\ \beta_i>0$. ... to achieve \(R_B(T)\le \varepsilon\) Algorithm~\ref{alg:f_ucb} requires at most $T$ iterations, where $T = 1+\sum_{i=1}^k \lceil(\frac{\beta_i}{\max\{f_i^*-f^*-\frac{\varepsilon}{2},\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\}})^{1/r}\rceil$.

results.notes: Table entry proved in Appendix B.2 from Lemma 1.
